name: Starter: Uzbek
about: Uzbek in real, everyday sentences, with each one's words in Uzbek order.

words.men: I (menga: to me, mening: my, meni: me)
words.siz: you (to a stranger, or more than one; sizda: at you, in your possession)
words.olmoq: take; after a verb's -a or -y: can
words.kun: day (har kuni: every day, shanba kuni: on Saturday)
words.sen: you (to a friend; senga: to you, seni: you)

items.text: Bitta choy va bitta suv, iltimos.
items.means: A tea and a water, please.
wrong: Bitta choylar va bitta suv, iltimos.
Bitta choy va bitta suvlar, iltimos.

items.means: My older brother is a student.
My older sister is a doctor.
Excuse me, where is the bathroom?
Excuse me, how much is this?
I live in a small house.
My mother goes to the city.
Excuse me, where is the train station?
Tomorrow I'll go to the city.

items.text: Mening bitta akam va bitta opam bor.
items.means: I have an older brother and an older sister.
wrong: Mening bitta akam va bitta opam yoʻq.
Men bitta akam va bitta opam bor.

items.means: My older brother lives in Tashkent.
My older sister doesn't speak English.
The children are playing in the yard.
The keys are on the table.
There's no milk in the fridge.
My mom is cooking in the kitchen.
We live in the city center.
The books are on the shelf.

items.text: Men har kuni ertalab choy ichaman.
wrong: Men har kuni ertalab choy ichadi.
Men har kuni ertalab choy ichmoq.

items.means: I drink my tea without sugar.
Do you take your coffee with milk?
Yesterday we ate at a restaurant.
There was no bread at the store.
I'd like to drink some tea.

items.text: Menga bir stakan suv bering, iltimos.
items.means: Could I have a glass of water, please?
wrong: Men bir stakan suv bering, iltimos.
Meni bir stakan suv bering, iltimos.

items.means: I go to work by bus.
The airport is far from here.
Tomorrow I'll take a taxi to the airport.
The pharmacy is next to the bank.
I'm going to the movies with my friend.
On Saturday we'll go to Samarkand.
We were at Charvak last summer.

concept.line: The verb normally follows its object and place: Men choy ichaman (I tea drink), Akam Toshkentda yashaydi (my-brother in-Tashkent lives).

After a noun or a place, -man, -san, -miz and -siz say I am, you are, we are and you are (polite): Men talabaman (I student-am), Siz talabasiz (you student-are); is usually has none (U talaba: he or she student), and -dir is formal or for emphasis.

words.means: oʻqituvchiman = I am a teacher; oʻqituvchi = teacher; oʻqituvchimisiz = are you a teacher?
talabamisiz = are you a student?; talabasiz = you are a student

concept.line: My and your are endings, often with mening or sening before the noun: mening ismim (my name-my), sening uying (your house-your), uning qizi (her daughter-her).

words.means: bor = there is; bormi = is there?

concept.line: -mi on a word makes a yes-or-no question (Inglizcha gapirasizmi?: English-ly do-you-speak?), and a question word stays where its answer goes: Siz qayerda yashaysiz?

words.means: gapirasizmi = do you speak?; gapiraman = I speak; gapirmaydi = does not speak
tushunmayman = I do not understand; tushunasizmi = do you understand?

concept.line: -a or -y with the person's ending says what you usually do, or will do: Men choy ichaman (I tea drink), Ertaga boramiz (tomorrow we-go).

words.means: uy = house; uyda = in a house; uydaman = I am at home; uyim = my house
yashayman = I live; yashaysiz = you live; yashaydi = lives
boraman = I go; boradi = goes; boryapsiz = you are going

concept.line: -da on the end says in or at: Toshkentda (in Tashkent), uyda (at home), maktabda (at school).

words.means: ishlayman = I work; ishlashim = my working
olmayman = to take; to be able to (auxiliary after a verb in -a/-y)
